name: Cognism
subcategory: B2B contact data and sales intelligence
tagline: A B2B prospecting database of company and contact records, including human-verified mobile numbers, with compliance screening baked in.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Cognism sells annual licences through sales with seat plus credit terms and does not publish list pricing.

verdictSummary: The software layer here is a search box over a table, and yes, an agent can build that before lunch. The product is not the search box, it is tens of millions of company and contact records, phone numbers that someone actually dialled to confirm, and a legal story about where every field came from. You cannot one-shot a dataset, and the parts of it you could assemble yourself by scraping are exactly the parts that get you a cease and desist or a GDPR complaint. There is a real consolation build: a local prospect tracker that holds the lists you already have and enriches them only from pages companies publish about themselves. It will not hand you a CRO's mobile number.
coreLoopDIY: A local prospect database that imports your existing CSVs, dedupes them, scrapes public contact and about pages on company websites for emails and phone numbers, and tracks outreach status per contact.
requirements: Your own seed list of companies or contacts to import
Patience with messy HTML and robots.txt
whatYouLose: The actual database: millions of contacts you did not have to source yourself
Phone-verified mobile numbers, which exist because humans called them, not because a regex found them
Compliance cover: notification workflows, do-not-call screening against regional registries, a defensible provenance trail
CRM and sequencer integrations that push records straight into Salesforce, HubSpot or Outreach
Intent signals, hiring and technographic filters, and refresh cycles that keep records from rotting
moatNotes: The GDPR and do-not-call posture is half the product in Europe. Plenty of buyers choose Cognism specifically so legal stops asking questions.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative to paying for contact data is paying a human to find contact data, and that human costs more per record and quits. Sales teams are buying coverage and reachability: a mobile number that connects on the first dial is worth more than ten guessed email patterns, and nobody is verifying numbers at scale in their spare time. The compliance layer matters too, especially for anyone selling into the EU, where sourcing your own scraped list is a genuine liability rather than a hypothetical one. The integrations seal it: data that does not land in the CRM automatically may as well not exist.
notes: The UI is a weekend; the records are not. The moat is a sourced, re-verified contact corpus plus the paperwork that makes using it legal in Europe.
prompt:
Build a local B2B prospect tracker called Leadbook. Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite via sqlite3 (no ORM), Jinja2 templates with htmx for interactions, plain CSS. Single process, runs with `uvicorn app:app --reload`, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

What it does:
1. CSV import: upload a CSV of companies or contacts, map columns in the browser, write to SQLite. Tables: companies (id, name, domain, country, notes), contacts (id, company_id, full_name, title, email, phone, source, source_url, added_at), outreach (id, contact_id, channel, status, note, occurred_at).
2. Dedupe on import: match companies by normalised domain, contacts by lowercased email, and flag probable duplicates by fuzzy name plus company for manual merge.
3. Public-page enrichment: given a company domain, fetch https://{domain} and look for links whose text or href suggests contact, about, team, imprint, impressum, or legal. Fetch up to 5 such pages. Respect robots.txt using urllib.robotparser, set a clear User-Agent, cap at 1 request per second per host, and timeout at 10 seconds. Extract emails and phone numbers with regex, store each with the exact source_url it came from. Never guess or pattern-generate an email that was not literally found on a page.
4. Prospect list view: filter by country, title keyword, has-email, has-phone, outreach status. Server-rendered table, htmx for inline status updates.
5. Outreach log: per contact, append a dated note with channel and status from a fixed set (queued, sent, replied, bounced, do-not-contact). Setting do-not-contact hard-excludes the contact from every export and list view thereafter.
6. CSV export of the current filtered view.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build or fake these: scraping LinkedIn or any logged-in service, buying or bundling any contact dataset, email pattern guessing, sending email, intent data, CRM sync.

Config in .env: USER_AGENT, REQUEST_TIMEOUT, DB_PATH. Ship a .env.example, a seeds.csv with 5 fake rows, and a README that states plainly that this tool holds data you supply or that companies publish about themselves, and that the user is responsible for lawful basis and for honouring suppression lists.

Write pytest tests for the dedupe logic, the robots.txt gate, and the do-not-contact exclusion.
